title: Special Topics in Art History and Archaeology; Identities and Modernism
description: Students will survey art and visual culture of the 19th and early-20th centuries with a focus on Europe and the United States. Examine the role modern art played in the construction of sexuality as a facet of identity, and in the representation of modern masculinity, femininity, and androgyny. Investigate how via modern art, identities were defined, challenged, exploited, and experienced. The issues considered in this course include gender and sexuality, race and representation, pseudo-science, and LGBTQ+ history.
